📊 Key hCG levels to know after embryo transfer:
🔹 Less than 5 mIU/mL → Negative for pregnancy
🔹 Greater than 20 mIU/mL → Positive — pregnancy likely

🔹 Day 14 after transfer → Above 200 mIU/mL suggests a continuing pregnancy

Diagnosed with a bulky uterus and worried about your chances of conceiving? You're asking the right questions — and the answers may be more hopeful than you think.

A normal uterus measures approximately 7–8 cm long & 4 cm thick. When it enlarges beyond this due to an underlying condition, it's termed a "bulky uterus."

⚠️ Common causes of a bulky uterus:
🔴 Fibroids — Non-cancerous tumours causing heavy bleeding & pelvic pain
🔴 Adenomyosis — Uterine lining growing into uterine muscle
🔴 Endometrial Cancer — Causing postmenopausal or abnormal bleeding
🔴 Pyometra — Pus accumulation due to uterine infection

→ Heavy or prolonged periods

Thin Endometrium Lining? Here's How We Treat It at FertilTree for Better IVF Results 🏥

Your uterine lining is the very foundation of a successful pregnancy. When it's too thin, even the best embryo may struggle to implant.

At FertilTree – Jaslok Hospital, Mumbai, our specialists diagnose and treat thin endometrium with precision — giving your IVF cycle the best possible environment to succeed.

📏 What is "thin" endometrium?
An ideal uterine lining is 8mm to 12mm thick. Below 8mm significantly reduces implantation chances.

⚠️ Signs you may have a thin endometrial lining:
🔴 Difficulty conceiving or repeated IVF failures
🔴 Light or scanty menstrual bleeding
🔴 Irregular or unusually short periods
🔴 History of miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy

What causes it?
→ Low estrogen levels
→ Decreased blood flow to the uterus
→ Uterine infections (including TB-related)
→ Previous D&C, surgery or Caesarean section
→ Long-term use of Clomiphene or mini-pills

पुरुषों में सेक्स ड्राइव और स्पर्म क्वालिटी का संबंध

कम सेक्स ड्राइव (लिबिडो) स्पर्म क्वालिटी को सीधे प्रभावित नहीं करती, लेकिन कम संभोग से ओव्यूलेशन मिस हो सकता है। तनाव, धूम्रपान, मोटापा, टेस्टोस्टेरोन कम होने से लिबिडो और स्पर्म दोनों प्रभावित। व्यायाम, अच्छी डाइट (जिंक, विटामिन D), और तनाव कम करने से सुधार। पुरुष भी फर्टिलिटी जांच कराएं।

सेक्स के बाद कितनी देर लेटना चाहिए प्रेग्नेंसी के लिए?

सेक्स के बाद 10-20 मिनट लेटे रहना स्पर्म को सर्वाइव करने और गर्भाशय में जाने में मदद करता है। वैज्ञानिक रूप से जरूरी नहीं, लेकिन हानिरहित है। पैर ऊपर रखना या कुशन से हिप्स उठाना बेहतर। ज्यादा देर (1 घंटा+) की जरूरत नहीं। आरामदायक रहें—तनाव से बचें।

सेक्स पोजीशन जो गर्भधारण में मदद करती हैं

मिशनरी, डॉगी स्टाइल या स्पूनिंग जैसी पोजीशन्स स्पर्म को गर्भाशय की ओर आसानी से पहुंचाती हैं। ग्रैविटी मदद करती है। कोई पोजीशन "गारंटीड" नहीं, लेकिन गहराई और आराम महत्वपूर्ण। सेक्स के बाद पीठ के बल लेटकर पैर ऊपर उठाएं। मुख्य बात टाइमिंग और नियमितता है—पोजीशन से ज्यादा फर्टाइल विंडो मायने रखती है।

प्रेग्नेंसी के लिए कितनी बार सेक्स करना चाहिए?

जaldi प्रेग्नेंट होने के लिए महीने में 10-15 बार संभोग आदर्श है, खासकर फर्टाइल दिनों में हर 1-2 दिन। ज्यादा फ्रीक्वेंसी (रोजाना) स्पर्म काउंट कम कर सकती है, जबकि बहुत कम (हफ्ते में 1-2 बार) ओव्यूलेशन मिस हो सकता है। व्यस्त जीवनशैली में शेड्यूल बनाएं। सेक्स केवल प्रजनन के लिए नहीं, बल्कि बॉन्डिंग के लिए भी जरूरी है। तनाव कम रखें—यह फर्टिलिटी बढ़ाता है।

गर्भधारण के लिए सेक्स करने का सही समय और दिन

गर्भ ठहराने के लिए सबसे महत्वपूर्ण है ओव्यूलेशन के आसपास (फर्टाइल विंडो) संभोग करना। महिलाओं के मासिक चक्र में ओव्यूलेशन आमतौर पर पीरियड्स शुरू होने के 12-16 दिन बाद होता है। इस दौरान सेक्स करने से गर्भधारण की संभावना 20-30% तक बढ़ जाती है। ऐप्स, ओव्यूलेशन कैलकुलेटर या बेसल बॉडी टेम्परेचर से ट्रैक करें। हर 2-3 दिन में संभोग रखें ताकि स्पर्म हमेशा उपलब्ध रहें। सेक्स के बाद 10-15 मिनट लेटना मददगार हो सकता है। PCOS या अनियमित पीरियड्स में डॉक्टर से जांच कराएं।

Menopause Is Not the End — It's a New Chapter
Menopause is a natural biological transition, yet for many women, it arrives accompanied by confusion, discomfort, and a concerning lack of reliable medical guidance. At Dr. Tanushree Pandey's clinic in South Mumbai, we believe every woman deserves clear information and supportive care through every stage of her reproductive life — including and beyond menopause.

Menopause is confirmed after 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period, typically between ages 45 and 55. The years leading up to it — perimenopause — can begin as early as the mid-30s, bringing with them a range of symptoms that are often attributed to stress, ageing, or other causes.

Common symptoms of perimenopause and menopause:
• Hot flashes and night sweats
• Irregular or heavy periods (in perimenopause)
• Sleep disturbances
• Mood changes, anxiety, or low mood
• Vaginal dryness and discomfort during intercourse
• Reduced libido
• Urinary frequency or leakage
• Cognitive changes, including difficulty concentrating
• Bone density loss (increasing risk of osteoporosis)

These symptoms are real, and they are treatable. Options range from lifestyle modifications and non-hormonal therapies to Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT), which — when appropriately prescribed — is safe and highly effective for most women.
At Dr. Pandey's clinic, menopause care is individualised, evidence-based, and delivered with the sensitivity this important life stage deserves.

Cervical Cancer Awareness: Prevention Saves Lives
Cervical cancer is one of the most preventable cancers — and yet it remains the second most common cancer among women in India. The reason this statistic persists is not lack of treatment; it is lack of awareness and access to screening.

Cervical cancer is caused almost entirely by persistent infection with high-risk strains of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) — a common virus transmitted through sexual contact. Critically, HPV infection often causes no symptoms at all, which is why regular screening is so essential.

What every woman should know:

PAP Smear: A cervical screening test that detects abnormal cells before they become cancerous. Recommended every 3 years from age 21, or every 5 years with combined HPV testing from age 30.

HPV Vaccination: Highly effective vaccines are available that protect against the most common cancer-causing HPV strains. Ideally given before sexual debut, but beneficial up to age 45 in many cases. Vaccination + screening together provide the strongest protection.

Warning signs to never ignore: unusual vaginal discharge (watery, foul-smelling, or blood-tinged), bleeding between periods or after intercourse, pelvic pain, and pain during intercourse.

When detected early, cervical cancer is highly treatable. When detected late, outcomes are significantly poorer. The difference, in most cases, is a simple, painless screening test.

Endometriosis: The Condition That Takes Too Long to Diagnose
Endometriosis affects approximately 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide — yet on average, it takes 7 to 10 years to receive a correct diagnosis. This delay is not just frustrating — it allows the condition to progress, causing increasing pain, damage to reproductive organs, and reduced fertility potential.

So what is endometriosis? It is a condition in which tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus — on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, bladder, bowel, and other surrounding structures. Each month, this tissue responds to hormonal changes just as the uterine lining does — swelling, breaking down, and bleeding — but with nowhere to go. This causes inflammation, the formation of scar tissue (adhesions), and often, intense pain.

Key symptoms to watch for:
• Severe menstrual cramps that worsen over time
• Chronic pelvic pain, not just during periods
• Pain during or after sexual intercourse
• Painful bowel movements or urination, especially during menstruation
• Heavy or irregular periods
• Difficulty conceiving

Endometriosis is frequently dismissed as "bad periods" — both by women themselves and sometimes by healthcare providers. If you have experienced any of these symptoms for more than a few cycles, a thorough gynaecological assessment is essential.

Having diabetes doesn’t mean you can’t conceive. It means your fertility journey needs the right preparation. 🌻💛

Uncontrolled blood sugar levels can impact fertility in both men and women:

• Men: reduced sperm count, poor motility, and increased sperm DNA fragmentation

What’s often missed is this: better glucose control is directly linked to better fertility outcomes for both partners.

Before trying to conceive, it helps to:
🌻 Optimise blood sugar levels and HbA1c (as advised by your doctor)
🌻 Consult both an endocrinologist and a fertility specialist
🌻 Review medications, nutrition, and lifestyle factors that affect reproductive health

Technology can play a big role too. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), insulin pumps, and fertility tracking tools now allow safer, more predictable conception planning.

This Men’s Health Month, let’s make space for conversations that feel easier to start.

Health discussions, especially around fertility and reproductive health, are often delayed because they feel confusing, uncomfortable, or overwhelming.

But clarity, openness, and understanding can make a meaningful difference. When people feel informed instead of intimidated, they are more likely to seek answers early and take confident steps towards their health.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe empathy begins with making every health conversation feel simple, transparent, and easier to navigate.

Male fertility is often overlooked until the journey to parenthood takes longer than expected.

But fertility is not only about sperm count. Sperm quality, including movement and overall health, can also play an important role in conception.
Advanced techniques like Microfluidics help select healthier moving sperm during IVF treatment, supporting a more personalised approach to fertility care.
This Men's Health Month, let's encourage earlier conversations, timely evaluations, and greater awareness around male fertility health.

Some dreams take a little longer to come true.

They begin as quiet hopes, become whispered prayers, and one day turn into the most beautiful reality.
This Father’s Day, we’re celebrating every dad who held on to hope, believed through the waiting, and never gave up on his dream of a family.

A diagnosis of azoospermia can feel overwhelming, especially when a semen analysis shows no sperm. For many men, it may seem like the end of the road to fatherhood.

However, in some cases, sperm may still be present within the testes and can sometimes be retrieved through specialised procedures such as TESA, TESE or Micro-TESE. These retrieved sperm may then be used in IVF/ICSI treatment, offering some couples an opportunity to pursue pregnancy using their own sperm and eggs.
This Men’s Health Month, let’s remember that the right diagnosis and expert evaluation can make all the difference.

Father's Day: AI Now Reading Sperm, Giving Hope of Fatherhood to Infertile Men
Dr. PGL Lalit Kumar, Head of Embryology and Scientific Director, Nova IVF Fertility

AI is revolutionizing sperm analysis in fertility clinics by offering more accurate and consistent assessments. While AI aids in identifying rare sperm cells and improving treatment outcomes, experts stress it should complement, not replace, clinical expertise. The adoption of AI in fertility care is increasing, enhancing the precision and efficiency of evaluations.

This Men’s Health Month, it’s important to remember that a man’s health extends beyond just himself.

Physical health, emotional well-being, lifestyle habits, and reproductive health can all influence not only his own future, but also the well-being of his partner and the family he hopes to build.
Small everyday choices, timely health check-ups, and greater awareness can make a meaningful difference over time. Prioritising health today is also an investment in healthier tomorrows for the generations ahead.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe conversations around fertility and reproductive health should include men equally because awareness and early action matter for everyone involved.

Sometimes, supporting your fertility doesn’t require long hours at the gym, just a few intentional moments through the day. Even short bursts of movement can begin to make a difference to how your body responds

Exercise snacking,” or quick intervals of activity, is linked to better hormone balance, improved circulation, and lower stress levels. When done consistently, these small efforts can support your body more effectively than a sedentary routine.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we guide you towards simple, sustainable habits that work with your lifestyle, helping you move forward, one step at a time.

Around 15–20 eggs begin developing in your ovaries each month.

But the body naturally selects just one dominant egg and asks the rest to stop growing.
This is a normal biological process, not a limitation.
In IVF, this process is supported differently, allowing multiple eggs to continue developing for better chances of conception.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe awareness of your body helps you make more informed fertility choices.

Sometimes what feels like falling behind is just the body and mind taking a different path than expected.

There are moments in the fertility journey when things feel uncertain, when progress feels slow, and when answers do not come easily.
But with the right guidance, clarity slowly replaces confusion and support makes all the difference.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we focus on bringing structure to that uncertainty through informed decisions, scientific analysis, personalised support and expert guidance.

Fertility puzzle: Why countries can't seem to reverse falling birth rates
Mr. Shobhit Agarwal, Chief Executive officer (CEO), Nova IVF Fertility

Countries facing falling birth rates are increasingly offering baby bonuses, cash incentives, tax breaks, childcare support, and housing benefits to encourage parenthood. However, evidence shows that financial incentives alone have limited long-term impact. Experts suggest broader reforms for affordable childcare; flexible work policies, gender equality, and family-friendly environments are more effective in addressing demographic decline.
